objective: Complete the Phase 10 folder-inference workflow by letting users deterministically save the exact mixed per-image results they see as versioned JSON or fixed-schema CSV, with safe writes, GUI lifecycle preservation, and real CPU end-to-end verification.
completion_conditions: All three checkpoint required-test allowlists and Codex verifiers PASS with no checkpoint exceeding one rework, one maker continuation, or one transient API retry, and no verifier mutation or checkpoint-scope violation.

The exact existing FolderInferenceResult is serialized without inference reruns or prediction recomputation into versioned deterministic JSON and fixed-header CSV, preserving item order, Unicode, partial failures, aggregate counts, and documented numeric/probability formats.

CSV and JSON destinations use safe same-directory replacement semantics, reject invalid formats and destinations explicitly, and preserve an existing destination on pre-replace failure without fallback paths or leftover successful-run temporary files.

InferencePage exports only its current completed folder aggregate, disables or clears export across initial, Running, fatal-failure, stale, and mode-transition states, handles dialog cancellation and bounded write errors on the GUI thread, and preserves Phase 10 async lifecycle and MainWindow close coordination.

A real CPU MainWindow integration processes valid and corrupt supported images through the established portable bundle, exports both formats, proves displayed/exported equivalence and partial-failure retention, and reruns without stale or duplicate output.

Existing single-image and folder inference APIs, result types, controller/worker contracts, portable training artifact paths and formats, launcher, dependencies, strict-marker registry, and non-export behavior remain compatible and unchanged outside the seven allowed files.

Phase 11 documentation and README accurately describe schemas, ordering, failure and write behavior, compatibility, and limitations without claiming import, progress, cancellation, preview, drag-and-drop, parallel execution, packaging, installer, TorchScript migration, CUDA validation, or later-Phase work.

The full project harness runs exactly once after all checkpoint approvals and passes without HEAD, staged-index, protected-file, allowed-scope, worktree, or harness mutation; the Phase then stops without planner, later Phase, add, commit, push, or pull-request operations.
